Mobile and Exact SDKs

Send events from your app to your own Birdwatch collector. Copy the project write key from Setup and use a collector address your device can reach.

React Native

Download React Native SDK ↓

Install the tarball and AsyncStorage 2.x. In Expo projects the following commands install the matching storage and UUID helpers.

npx expo install expo-crypto @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
npm install ./birdwatch-react-native-0.2.0.tgz

import { createReactNativeClient } from "@birdwatch/react-native";
import { randomUUID } from "expo-crypto";

type Events = { checkout_completed: { orderId: string; total: number } };
const analytics = await createReactNativeClient<Events>({
  host: "https://analytics.example.com", writeKey: "YOUR_PROJECT_WRITE_KEY", randomUUID,
});

await analytics.identify("user-42");
const { id } = await analytics.enqueue("checkout_completed",
  { orderId: "order-123", total: 54 }, { id: "checkout:order-123" });
// The checkout is saved locally. Navigation can continue while delivery is pending.
await analytics.reset(); // Queued events retain the identity used at capture.

Create one client per project at app startup and retain it while collection is enabled. React Native uses AsyncStorage by default. You can supply an adapter with async getItem and setItem. Pass storage: null for an ephemeral client. A secure randomUUID option is required on hosts without crypto.randomUUID.

enqueue resolves with the event ID after a local commit. capture and screen also save before sending and resolve with a collector receipt. A transient delivery error can reject those calls while the event remains queued. Pass a stable occurrence ID when retrying an application action. For explicit screen tracking, call await analytics.screen("Checkout").

The client replays pending events on launch and AppState transitions. While it can execute, a retry timer backs off to one minute. If your app already observes connectivity, pass subscribeConnectivity: listener => NetInfo.addEventListener(state => listener(state.isInternetReachable === true)) to wake it immediately. Terminating the app preserves its queue. Reopening it resumes delivery.

flush() attempts delivery of outstanding events. shutdown() removes listeners and attempts a final drain. A failed drain preserves pending events. HTTP 400 and 413 for an individual event are terminal input errors. Authentication failures leave queued events available for retry with the same project configuration. Use onError to observe failed transport attempts.

Each collector and write key has a separate queue. Its default capacity is 1,000 events with a 1 MiB serialized limit. New writes reject on overflow or storage failure. Earlier entries stay in place. maxQueueSize, batchSize, flushIntervalMs, maxRetries, and timeoutMs tune delivery.

Expo Exact

Download Expo Exact SDK ↓

Install the release tarball beside your Exact app’s package.json.

npm install ./birdwatch-exact-0.2.0.tgz

The included example/ contains an app manifest, Contract view, and TypeScript answers. Copy the three files into your Exact app and replace the host and write key. The example grants access to the collector origin and one SQLite file. Pressing Record completion commits an event to the device. A launch task, a post-save action and a ten-second Contract task invoke replay while the app is running.

import { createExactClient } from "@birdwatch/exact";
import type { Sources } from "./app.contract.d.ts";

const host = "https://analytics.example.com";
export const grants = `net.fetch ${host}\nsqlite.open app:/data/birdwatch.sqlite`;
const analytics = createExactClient({ host, writeKey: "YOUR_PROJECT_WRITE_KEY", fetch });

const sources: Sources = {
  recordCompletion: ([distinctId, id, at], _store, storage) =>
    analytics.enqueue({
      id, distinctId, event: "onboarding_completed",
      timestamp: new Date(at).toISOString(),
    }, storage.sqlite),
  replay: (_args, _store, storage) => analytics.flush(storage.sqlite),
};

Pass the action’s occurrence time from Contract to the data answer. The sample uses time.epochAtZero + performanceNow(). enqueue takes a stable occurrence ID and returns { id } once SQLite commits. Retrying the same pending ID preserves its first payload. Each collector and write key has a separate 1,000-event limit. Overflow and local storage failure reject the enqueue.

flush sends up to 100 pending events per call. Successful and duplicate acknowledgements remove their corresponding rows. A transport error retains the row. A definitive HTTP 400 or 413 retires the individual rejected event and surfaces the error. Call replay from your host's tasks on launch and periodically to resume after reconnection. The database survives a process restart.

The direct APIs remain available. capture sends one event and captureBatch sends 1–100 events in one request. They return collector counts and use the collector clock when no timestamp is supplied. Use enqueue for durable offline collection.

The example targets Expo Exact at bb3c00b.

Swift

Download Swift SDK ↓

Unzip birdwatch-swift-0.2.0.zip. In Xcode, choose File → Add Package Dependencies → Add Local, select the folder containing Package.swift, and add the Birdwatch product to your target. In SwiftPM, use .package(path: "../Birdwatch") and add .product(name: "Birdwatch", package: "Birdwatch") to your target.

import Foundation
import Birdwatch

let analytics = try BirdwatchClient(
    host: URL(string: "https://analytics.example.com")!,
    writeKey: "YOUR_PROJECT_WRITE_KEY"
)
try await analytics.identify("user-42")
let id = try await analytics.enqueue("checkout_completed",
    properties: ["orderId": "order-123", "total": 54], id: "checkout:order-123")
await analytics.reset()

Keep a client alive from app startup. enqueue returns the event ID after SQLite commits the original timestamp, identity and properties. It works offline. capture and screen also persist before sending and return a collector receipt. A transient failure can throw while the event stays queued. flush() explicitly attempts pending delivery. Use the same occurrence ID for application-level retries.

On iOS 15+ and macOS 12+, the client automatically drains at startup, when Network.framework reports a usable path, and on a retry timer while the process can execute. A device that reconnects while the app is terminated syncs on its next launch. The collector treats an already accepted ID as a successful duplicate acknowledgement.

The default database lives in Application Support/Birdwatch and is excluded from backup. Queues and identities are scoped to the collector and project write key. Identity changes affect subsequent events. Set persistence: .memory to keep both ephemeral, or pass an outboxURL to explicitly select a disk database. Each project holds up to maxQueueSize pending events (default 1,000). Full queues and write failures throw without evicting older events.

Per-request retries reuse the encoded body. Configure timeout in seconds and maxRetries for transient failures. HTTP 400 and 413 retire a rejected event. Other unsuccessful responses preserve it. An acknowledged event is removed only after the local deletion commits. A device must be able to reach its configured collector URL.

Run swift test from the package directory. Set BIRDWATCH_TEST_HOST and BIRDWATCH_TEST_KEY to exercise a live collector as well.

Android

Download Android SDK

The native Android SDK works from Kotlin and Java on Android 7.0 (API 24) and later. It uses Android’s SQLite, networking, and connectivity APIs and has no third-party runtime dependencies.

Save birdwatch-android-0.2.0.aar in your app module’s libs/ folder. Add it to app/build.gradle.kts and sync Gradle.

dependencies {
    implementation(files("libs/birdwatch-android-0.2.0.aar"))
}

Create one client per project at application startup. Use the write key from Birdwatch Setup and an HTTPS collector URL your device can reach.

import dev.birdwatch.sdk.Birdwatch
import dev.birdwatch.sdk.Event

val analytics = Birdwatch.open(applicationContext, "https://analytics.example.com", writeKey)

// Call after sign-in. SDK operations submitted to this client run in order.
analytics.identify("user-42")
val checkout = Event("checkout_completed", mapOf("orderId" to "order-123", "total" to 54), "checkout:order-123")
analytics.enqueue(checkout).whenComplete { eventId, error ->
    if (error != null) android.util.Log.e("Analytics", "Could not save checkout", error)
}
Method Completion
enqueue(event) The event ID after the local SQLite transaction commits, including offline.
capture(event) A collector receipt with id, accepted, and duplicates. The SDK saves the event before sending.
screen(name) A collector receipt for a screen_view event.
identify(person), reset(), distinctId() Set, rotate, or read the project’s persistent identity. Earlier events keep their original identity.
flush() Delivery of the events outstanding when the flush reaches the local queue. A failed request completes the future exceptionally.
close() Stop work and release the client’s resources. Committed events remain available on the next open.

Methods that return a CompletableFuture work from Java as well. The SDK owns its storage and networking threads. To use collector receipts from Java:

analytics.capture("search", Collections.singletonMap("results", 3))
    .thenAccept(receipt -> Log.d("Analytics", "Acknowledged " + receipt.getId()));

Use asynchronous callbacks or your app’s coroutine integration for futures. Move UI updates onto the main thread. An Event snapshots its JSON properties and timestamp when constructed. Supply the same ID for application-level retries of one action, or let the SDK generate a UUID. To import an earlier occurrence, use Event(name, properties, id, timestampMillis). Properties can contain JSON primitives, string-keyed maps, lists, arrays, and null.

Offline delivery. The outbox lives in the app’s no-backup directory. Opening the client, a network availability callback, and a retry timer all trigger replay. If connectivity returns while the process is stopped, opening the client on its next launch resumes delivery. A lost acknowledgement can produce a second request with the same ID. Birdwatch records the occurrence once. HTTP 400 and 413 retire an invalid event. Failed authentication, transient responses, and malformed acknowledgements retain the event. The SDK honors Retry-After on 429 and 503.

Queue capacity defaults to 1,000 events per collector and write key. A full queue or storage failure rejects the new write and preserves existing entries. Configure Birdwatch.Builder(context, host, writeKey) with maxQueueSize, timeoutMillis (default 5,000), and onError to observe replay failures and rejected events.

Local development. Use http://10.0.2.2:8123 to reach a host-machine collector from the standard Android Emulator. If Android blocks cleartext HTTP, configure your debug build to allow it for the development endpoint. Use a device-reachable HTTPS address for deployed apps. The AAR declares the normal INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE permissions.

Build from source. In the source release, open sdks/android/ in Android Studio, or run ./gradlew assembleRelease there with JDK 17 and Android SDK Platform 35 installed. The AAR is written to build/outputs/aar/. Run ./gradlew connectedDebugAndroidTest with an emulator or test device connected. The SDK uses the Birdwatch MIT license. The Gradle wrapper’s license and notices are in gradle/wrapper/.
